Then "calculate the derivative of the resulting function and evaluate it at x=2". The resulting function after evaluating derivative at x=4 is a number. But maybe they mean take the derivative of the original polynomial again? Or maybe they want second derivative? After that, could you also calculate the derivative of the resulting function and evaluate it at x=2?" The "resulting function" might refer to the derivative function itself. So first derivative f'(x) = 9x^2 - 4x + 5. Evaluate at x=4 gives 9*16 - 4*4 + 5 = 144 - 16 + 5 = 133. Then "calculate the derivative of the resulting function" meaning derivative of f'(x) which is f''(x) = 18x - 4. Evaluate at x=2 gives 18*2 - 4 = 36 - 4 = 32. That seems plausible. Alternatively, they might want derivative of the evaluated result (a constant 133) which would be zero. But that seems trivial. So likely they want second derivative. We'll produce answer accordingly.
